facts.statement: The genus Parahongshanornis and its type species P. chaoyangensis were named by Li Li, Wang Jingqi, and Hou Shilin in 2011.
facts.quote: Parahongshanornis was first named by Li Li, Wang Jingqi and Hou Shilin in 2011 and the type species is Parahongshanornis chaoyangensis.

facts.statement: Parahongshanornis lived during the Aptian stage of the lower Cretaceous in what is now Liaoning Province, north-eastern China.
facts.quote: Parahongshanornis is an extinct genus of early bird from the lower Cretaceous (Aptian stage) of what is now Liaoning Province, north-eastern China.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen PMOL-AB00161 was found near Yuanjiawa, Chaoyang, in the Jiufotang Formation of the Jehol Biota, dating to about 120 million years ago.
facts.quote: Parahongshanornis is known from the holotype PMOL-AB00161, which was found near Yuanjiawa, Chaoyang, in the middle Aptian Jiufotang Formation of the Jehol Biota, about 120 million years old.

facts.statement: The known fossil consists of a nearly complete, articulated skeleton that lacks a skull but preserves soft tissue remains including feathers.
facts.quote: It consists of a nearly complete and articulated skeleton missing the skull but showing remains of the soft parts of the body, including some feathering.

facts.statement: Parahongshanornis was a small bird with a femur measuring twenty-four millimetres in length.
facts.quote: Parahongshanornis is a small species with a femur length of twenty-four millimetres.

facts.statement: The furcula of Parahongshanornis is U-shaped, and the coracoid is elongated with a broad end that touches the sternum.
facts.quote: The furcula is U-shaped. The coracoid is elongated but with a broad end touching the sternum.

facts.statement: Parahongshanornis was assigned to the family Hongshanornithidae based on comparative anatomy rather than cladistic analysis.
facts.quote: Parahongshanornis was assigned to the Hongshanornithidae, based on comparative anatomy rather than a cladistic analysis.

facts.statement: Parahongshanornis is considered the youngest known member of the family Hongshanornithidae.
facts.quote: It would be the youngest hongshanornithid known.

facts.statement: The time range for Parahongshanornis is estimated from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
